newsitem.title: UK: GOLF-LEHMAN LEADS UNFINISHED SECOND ROUND.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-LEHMAN LEADS UNFINISHED SECOND ROUND.

text.p: British Open champion Tom Lehman held a three-shot lead over fellow American Steve Jones when play finished after a five-hour weather delay in the second round of the Loch Lomond World Invitational on Thursday.
Thirty-seven players had still to complete their rounds on Friday before the halfway cut is made ahead of the third round. The weather forecast is favourable.
Lightning in the area forced the players off the course at 1515 local time (1415 GMT) and heavy rain prevented a resumption until 1800 (1700 GMT).
But without striking a shot they were forced to scurry off again when the threat of lightning suddenly returned.

They finally resumed at 2010 (1910 GMT) with Lehman, who has finished 11 holes when play was halted, completing a solid five- under-par 66 to go with his first-round 65 for an 11-under-par total of 131. He has not had a bogey in two rounds.

Jones, the 1996 U.S. Open champion and Lehman's playing partner in the American World Cup team that finished second last year, was closest on eight under par after a second round of 65 which he completed ahead of the suspension.
The two first round leaders, Englishman Paul Curry and Joakim Haeggman of Sweden, were seven under after 72s to go with their opening course-record 63s.

Greg Norman was another stroke behind following a second successive 68. One player, Welshman Paul Affleck, was disqualified after hitting a shot after the first klaxon sounded to cease play immediately.
U.S. Open champion Ernie Els and Colin Montgomerie were level on three under par.
Lehman's round lasted nine hours and 40 minutes including a four hour-55 minute delay. "Now that's a slow-play problem," he said.
"There's only so much you can do in the tent. But I feel really pleased with the way I played."
He said the worst thing was facing a awkward chip near the 12th green as his first shot after the break.
"It was about the hardest chip you can have on the course. I got it to 18 feet and holed it for a par," he said.
"I hit a bad drive at the 13th but got a par there too and after that I played pretty well.

"The fact that I have had no bogeys shows my concentration is good," added the popular American, who had only one practice round here because the plane bringing him from the United States was delayed.
His five birdies came on putts of 30, 15, 10 and eight feet twice.

Jones, who scored an 11-stroke victory in the Phoenix Open this year with a 26-under-par winning total, has gone off the boil since then, missing halfway cuts at the Players Championship, the Masters, the Heritage Classic and the Colonial events.
"It was all because of a swing fault I didn't know I had. I was taking the club inside too much on the backswing," he said.
He began his charge by rifling a two-iron approach to eight feet at the 505-yard third and holing the putt for an eagle, then had five birdies and one bogey.
The halfway cut looked likely to fall at one over par and there will be notable absentees from the final two rounds including Jose Maria Olazabal of Spain.
He was two over and will miss a cut for the first time in 11 events since he began his comeback from 18 months off with foot problems in February.

Bernhard Langer, who won two titles back-to-back this year, missed his fourth cut in five events while Ryder Cup captain Seve Ballesteros fell to his 10th missed cut in 12 events with a second successive 79.
Tournament director Mike Stewart said the event could still be completed on Saturday as scheduled if there was good weather the next two days.
He said there was no option to extend to Sunday because so many players were involved in final qualifying on Sunday and Monday for next week's British Open at Royal Troon.
